messages:
alice: quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-picker tweak i see a 10-15% p95/p99 increase on the mistral-1g canonical workload. looks correlated with requests that use the chat template + system prompt (lots of special tokens).
ben: can you paste the perf numbers and the canary id?
alice: canary id = canary-mistral-2026-03-17-3. baseline p95=120ms -> canary p95=136ms, p99=290ms -> 335ms. throughput steady. CPU/GPU util unchanged.
carol: any changes to batching heuristics or prefetch?
alice: we enabled a small aggressive prefetch window in kernel-picker (prefetch_k=8 -> 12) and narrowed the kernel choice threshold to prefer float16 kernels on short sequences. suspect kernel selection + byte-fallback interactions.
dan: interesting — if tokenizer emits a byte-fallback token run-length in the system prompt then sequence length jumps and we hit a different kernel path, plus KV prefetch might overestimate hop counts. did you repro with a minimal prompt?
alice: repro curl (shortened):
```
curl -s -X POST https://canary.api.redwood/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CANARY' \
  -d '{"model":"mistral-1g","input":"<system>\nYou are an assistant.\n</system>\nUser: hello"}'
```
carol: try forcing the new picker off (KERNEL_PICKER=legacy) and run the same set — that will tell us if it is picker vs tokenizer.
ben: ran locally with picker=legacy — p95 back to 118ms, p99 back to 288ms. so picker is implicated.
dan: i pulled pprof flamegraph from canary for a p99 trace: https://perf-grafana/fg/1876543210 — looks like a small hot spot in kv_cache::ensure_prefetch + kernel_selector::score_switch.
eve: also seeing traces where tokenizer emits series of <unk> replacements (byte-fallback) for some unicode sequences in the system prompt. could be pushing effective seq_len + changing head alignment.
alice: hypothesis: kernel-picker's prefetch_k increase combined with RoPE interpolation boundary for mixtral/mistral causes extra KV page faults and triggers the byte-fallback kernel which is slower. additionally, some model configs have head_dim != kv_dim assumptions and the new picker picks a kernel optimized for kv_dim alignment that is suboptimal for these prompts.
ben: can we gather a small set of failing prompt examples (system + user) and run them with: picker=canary|legacy, prefetch_k=8|12, HEAD_DIM_OVERRIDE? i'll script it.
carol: add a metric: count of byte-fallback occurrences per request and histogram of effective token_count after tokenizer post-processing. that will make the correlation clearer.
dan: short patch idea: restore old picker threshold for sequence lengths < 64 and keep aggressive for > 64. also clamp prefetch_k when byte-fallback detected. low-risk rollback.
ealice: agreed — can we try rollout: 1) patch to clamp prefetch on canary, 2) run 1k requests from the failing testset, 3) if p99 improves, ship and monitor.
perf-bot: deploy audit — patch branch: fix/prefetch-clamp-1876 deployed to canary (canary-mistral-2026-03-17-4) at 2026-03-17T18:12:05Z :rocket:
ben: ran 1k test requests against new canary: p95=122ms, p99=300ms — improvement vs previous canary but still slightly worse than baseline. byte-fallback rate dropped 65%.
dan: next steps: 1) add head_dim validation when selecting kernel (reject kernel that assumes different head/kv dims), 2) add a quick tokenizer check that flags system prompts with likely byte-fallback before picker runs, 3) instrument kv_cache prefetch hits/misses more granularly.
alice: ok i'll open the triage ticket with repro + logs + perf links and assign tasks. @ben please add the failing prompt corpus to the ticket. @carol can you own the metrics+dashboards?
carol: yep will add dashboard tiles for byte_fallback.count, kv_prefetch.misses, kernel_selector.choice.
eve: FYI oncall saw a user report about higher latency yesterday — i linked this thread in the incident. will update SLA channel once we have rollback/ship decision.
alice: thanks team. small note: avoid changing picker thresholds globally until we have head-dim checks in place.
ben: I'll PR the clamp and head-dim check today.
dan: I'll follow up with a microbenchmark isolating RoPE scaling boundary effects (interpolating attention cos/sin) to see if that contributes to kernel scoring.
alice: great. adding a quick TODO: script to reproduce with varied unicode/system-token permutations so we can run in CI.
perf-bot: triage ticket r-1234 created and linked to canary traces.
